rationale: A legal 4 ns source event can fit entirely between consecutive 20 ns destination edges, so both synchronizer stages miss it. No stretching, toggle, acknowledgment or rate contract preserves events.
caveats: Reproducible logical counterexample after settling: destination edges at 10 and 30 ns, source pulse from 12 through 16 ns (source edges 4+4n ns). Both samples are low. Back-to-back events may also merge. This is event loss despite adequate two-stage level topology.

author_reading.evidence_and_limits: 4 ns source vs 20 ns destination; one-source-cycle pulses and no event-rate bound/ack. Verify the contract permits pulses entirely between destination edges.

labels.rationale: A four-nanosecond pulse can rise and fall entirely between twenty-nanosecond destination edges; the two-stage level synchronizer then never observes it. Back-to-back source events can also merge. No rate limit, stretching, toggle or acknowledgment prevents loss.
labels.caveats: Two registers address metastability propagation, not event delivery. Unspecified startup also prevents treating initial pulse_d as meaningful; event loss exists after settling regardless.

labels.rationale: A source-cycle event lasts 4 ns while destination edges are 20 ns apart. A pulse strictly between two destination edges is never sampled, so neither p1 nor p2 records it. Consecutive source events can also merge. Two sampling stages do not preserve event count.
labels.caveats: No event-rate or pulse-width guarantee exists. Startup values are unspecified but the missed-event example can occur after arbitrarily long settling.
